data.narrative:
Qilimanjaro, a Series A quantum computing company, has raised $10M to date across a five-founder team. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 identifiable peers—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private entities including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable methodology here. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $20M. A peer-median approach, while theoretically sound, cannot be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the quantum computing universe—the existing peer set lacks the requisite density of datapoints at comparable valuation tiers to produce meaningful median anchoring.

The triangulated valuation range derived from applicable methods spans $17M (low) to $23M (median $20M), anchored entirely to stage-progression mechanics. This range reflects standard early-stage venture step-up conventions applied to disclosed fundraising. Material uncertainties include the absence of near-peer valuation benchmarks at identical stage and the nascent nature of quantum computing markets, which limits predictability of traditional stage-progression multiples. Investors should treat this range as indicative of near-term financing benchmarks rather than intrinsic value absent additional operational or technology data.
